title: HighDimensionalHighProbabilityStationarity.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective f on ℝᵈ may be nonconvex. Its gradient is globally L-Lipschitz, its infimum f⋆ is finite, and f(x₀) − f⋆ ≤ Δ. The infimum need not be attained.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at an adaptively chosen x returns only g(x, ξ) for a fresh i.i.d. real seed ξ. The jointly measurable map g satisfies E[g(x, ξ)] = ∇f(x). The algorithm knows d, L, σ, Δ, ε, δ, and x₀. It accesses the hidden objective through oracle replies, with g and the seed law also hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalHighProbabilityStationarity.lean, Params, toGeneral, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, and spec.Reply. LongTails/Setups/HighProbabilityStationarity.lean, spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x, E[‖g(x, ξ) − ∇f(x)‖²] ≤ σ², with σ ≥ 0. This second-moment condition permits heavy-tailed errors and includes σ = 0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries, replies, and outputs lie in Euclidean ℝᵈ. The regime requires L > 0, ε > 0, 2⁵⁴ε² ≤ LΔ, and d ≥ 2⁴⁰[1 + (LΔ/ε²)(1 + σ²/ε²)]⁴. The dimension threshold is independent of δ.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalHighProbabilityStationarity.lean, toGeneral, spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.Output, and spec.valid.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns one measurable point X in ℝᵈ. Success is evaluated at that output by the unsquared Euclidean gradient norm ‖∇f(X)‖ ≤ ε.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: With a fixed oracle-call budget, the output must satisfy P(‖∇f(X)‖ ≤ ε) ≥ 1 − δ for every admissible instance, where 0 < δ ≤ 1/4. The probability includes the independent algorithm and oracle randomness.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalHighProbabilityStationarity.lean, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/Setups/HighProbabilityStationarity.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/Template.lean, executeWithTrace and Convergence.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Finding an ε-stationary point of a smooth, lower-bounded objective with an unbiased, bounded-variance stochastic gradient is a standard oracle-complexity benchmark. This formulation specifies the output confidence and the dimension regime for a randomized lower bound.

descriptionHtml:
High-Dimensional Stationarity with High Probability

We seek an approximately stationary point of a possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R in high dimension d. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz for L>0, and the objective value at a given starting point x0 is within Δ of the finite infimum. At each query, the oracle uses a fresh independent sample to return an unbiased gradient estimate with mean squared error at most σ2, where σ≥0. Given a tolerance ε>0 and a failure probability 0<δ≤1/4, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈Rd satisfying ∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε with probability at least 1−δ.

Write f⋆ for the value of the optimization problem infx∈Rdf(x), and use the Euclidean norm throughout. The algorithm receives d, L, σ, Δ, ε, δ, and x0. The gap bound Δ and the dimension d∈N lie in the regime LΔ≥254ε2,d≥240(1+LΔε2(1+σ2ε2))4.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and initial gap). The function f is differentiable on Rd, and for all x,y∈Rd, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥. Its infimum f⋆ is finite and satisfies f(x0)−f⋆≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Stochastic gradient oracle). On call k at any x∈Rd, the oracle returns g(x,ξk), where g:Rd×R→Rd is jointly measurable. The real-valued samples (ξk)k≥0 are independent with common law ν, and the sequence is independent of the algorithm’s randomness. For each x∈Rd and ξ∼ν, the vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable, the squared error ∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable, and Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and satisfy P(∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε)≥1−δ, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle samples.

theorems.formulaHtml: ⌊L⋅Δ⋅(1+σ2ε2)+σ2⋅log⁡(1δ⋅14)254⋅ε2⌋+

comparisonHtml:
Let f:Rd→R have an L-Lipschitz gradient and f(x0)−inff≤Δ, with L>0 and ε>0. The jointly measurable stochastic gradient uses IID real seeds, is unbiased, and has variance at most σ2 (σ≥0). The target for a measurable output x^ is Pr(∥∇f(x^)∥≤ε)≥1−δ. The setup requires 0<δ≤1/4, LΔ≥254ε2, and d≥240(1+B)4.

Necessary budgets for high-dimensional high-probability stationarity
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) HighProbabilityStationarityLowerBound (Ours) (review) Lower bound: Ω(B+σ2ε2ℓ) stochastic gradient calls
(2) Derived bound (Arjevani et al. 2023; Carmon et al. 2020), Thm. 3, Eq. (23) (K=1), and Thm. 2 (p=1), respectively Lower bound: Ω(B) calls at δ<1/2, ε≤cLΔ. The probability bounds in the proofs give the common criterion. The noiseless term holds even with values and all derivatives, and the noisy term with values and stochastic gradients. (1): Adds σ2ℓ/ε2 to the necessary budget. It exceeds B for σ>0 and ℓ>LΔ/ε2+LΔ/σ2. At σ=ε, this means δ<14e−2LΔ/ε2. Formalizes the probability lower bound for arbitrary randomized algorithms. (1): Requires δ≤1/4 and a larger dimension threshold. In (2), dimension O~((LΔ/ε2)2(1+σ2/ε2)) suffices.

Abbr: B=LΔε2(1+σ2ε2), ℓ=log⁡(1/(4δ)), c>0 is a universal constant, and O~ suppresses logarithmic factors.

Arjevani, Yossi, Yair Carmon, John C. Duchi, Dylan J. Foster, Nathan Srebro, and Blake Woodworth. 2023. “Lower Bounds for Non-Convex Stochastic Optimization.” Mathematical Programming 199: 165–214. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-022-01822-7.
Carmon, Yair, John C. Duchi, Oliver Hinder, and Aaron Sidford. 2020. “Lower Bounds for Finding Stationary Points I.” Mathematical Programming 184: 71–120. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-019-01406-y.
source:
import LongTails.Setups.HighProbabilityStationarity
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.InnerProductSpace
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalHighProbabilityStationarity

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  L : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  δ : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

noncomputable def toGeneral (q : Params) : LongTails.Setups.HighProbabilityStationarity.Params where
  E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Ω := ℝ
  L := q.L
  σ := q.σ
  Δ := q.Δ
  ε := q.ε
  δ := q.δ
  x0 := q.x0

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) → ℝ
  Query q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Reply q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Output q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧ 0 < q.δ ∧ q.δ ≤ 1 / 4 ∧
    2 ^ 54 * q.ε ^ 2 ≤ q.L * q.Δ ∧
    2 ^ 40 * (1 + q.L * q.Δ * (1 + q.σ ^ 2 / q.ε ^ 2) / q.ε ^ 2) ^ 4 ≤ (q.d : ℝ)
  admissible q f O :=
    LongTails.Setups.HighProbabilityStationarity.spec.admissible (toGeneral q) f O
  successful q f output P :=
    LongTails.Setups.HighProbabilityStationarity.spec.successful (toGeneral q) f output P

end LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalHighProbabilityStationarity
